tasks.behavior: The server prepares, checks and tracks sends and transfers from profile wallets
acceptance: An owner with a fresh sign-in prepares a send or transfer; members, keys and stale sign-ins are refused (R-211)
Invalid, zero, token-contract and own-wallet recipients, too-large amounts and failed dry runs are refused; contract and first-send warnings and the network fee are returned (R-211, D-119)

A reported hash moves a send to Sending and the watcher's matching transfer to Sent, then final; a reorg returns it to Sending; a revert or a hash with no transaction for 30 minutes fails it; an unreported send expires after 10 minutes; a signed hash is never lost (R-212)
openapi.yaml and api.md describe the send routes
notes: 2026-11-05 review pass by reviewer: Re-reviewed 6bf76643..fb99e8cc. All four must-fix items are fixed: openapi lists money.move; only the watcher's transfer makes a send sent, and R-212, api.md and acceptance 3 match; a new test covers a reorg going back to sending and then dropped; api.md lists POST /sends as an Idempotency-Key exception with the reason. The notes are fixed too: a hash is kept in prepared, expired and canceled; sends_tx makes a hash belong to one send; refused() counts only reverts; the log is redacted; toProfileId is lowercased; an API test refuses a key and money.move as a key scope. go test -race on internal/send and httpapi/tests passes. Minor, not blocking: openapi.yaml:2981 still lists 409 send_in_progress for submit, which Submit no longer returns. docs/backend/architecture.md:252 still says one open send per wallet and chain; it is now one unsigned send. The FOR UPDATE wallet lock in keep() (prepare.go:206) does not cover Submit, so a prepare racing a submit can leave two signed sends in flight. Each was signed by the user, so this is harmless.

2026-11-05 review pass by reviewer: Re-reviewed 6bf76643..f2dbb0e8. Both match the code. go test -race on internal/send and httpapi/tests passes; no Go code changed after that run. Known and accepted: the FOR UPDATE wallet lock in keep() does not cover Submit, so a prepare racing a submit can leave two signed sends in flight. Each one was signed by the user.

2026-11-06 review pass by reviewer: Fresh review of 19c49d8f..f0633a37. Since the passing review (f2dbb0e8) only docs/tasks.json changed: f0633a37 records that review, and the uncommitted change is the 2026-11-06 verify record. No code changed. Read send/, sendapi/, the 00097 migration, the guards, openapi.yaml and api.md. Amounts are base units, positive and capped at the balance. Recipients are refused when invalid, zero, a token contract or the own wallet, and a bad checksum is refused. A transfer looks up the other profile's wallet on the server. The dry run is from the wallet. Contract and new-recipient warnings and a 0 fee paid by forwend are returned. One unsigned send per wallet and chain is kept by a unique index and the wallet row lock. Only a confirmed or detected wallet_transfers row matching hash, wallet, token, recipient and amount makes a send sent; a receipt alone never does. sends_tx gives each hash one send, and a hash is kept for prepared, canceled and expired sends. Prepare needs FreshSignIn(money.move); get, submit and cancel need Can(money.move). No role or key scope has money.move. openapi.yaml and api.md list all four routes. Ran: go test ./internal/send/ ./internal/httpapi/tests/ -count=1 (both ok); check-docs.py (0 errors). Minor, not blocking: api.md says a submit takes its hash in any state but sent and failed. A submitted send takes only its own hash again; another hash is refused. Known and accepted: Submit is not under the wallet lock, so two signed sends can be in flight at once.

notes: 2026-11-06 review pass by reviewer: Pass. Money path is sound: Privy signs transfer(send.to, send.amount) on send.token and send.chainId, all from the server's send, which matchesRequest compares to the request (chain, token, amount, recipient) before the review shows; the review shows those same values; amounts stay bigint/base units. The sheet locks (Escape, backdrop, Close, Back) while signing and until a server read holds the hash; a lost submit is re-sent on each 1.5 s read. Send/Transfer only for money.move (owner only, backend enforces too); Transfer only with another owner profile with a wallet. Minor, not blocking: (1) send-review.tsx:83 calls onSigning(false) right after onSubmitted, so the sheet is unlocked for one frame before SendProgress sets holding; drop that call and let progress own the lock. (2) matchesRequest does not check send.from against the profile wallet (lib/send.ts:55, send-sheet.tsx:199). (3) No unit test covers the lock or the re-report of a lost hash; only lib functions and the live run. (4) PROJECT.md:298 R-213 still says the button reads Send; it names the amount and reads Transfer for a transfer. (5) feeText shows a non-zero fee in the sent token's units (marked; unreachable while sendable = gas_sponsored). (6) If the server never takes the hash, the progress step stays locked with Done disabled. Ran: vitest src/features/send (5 passed); harness check typecheck lint docs-check (all passed).

tasks.behavior: A signed send shows as a Sending row in the money lists until the watcher records it
acceptance: The server lists a profile's signed sends with no recorded transfer, bringing each up to date (R-215)
Transactions and Recent transactions show them first as Sending rows, and read again when a send is signed (R-215)
notes: 2026-11-06 review fail by reviewer: Fail on one test fix; the code itself is right. Backend: GET /v1/profiles/{id}/sends uses g.Can(money.read), the same as transactions. It reads only this profile's submitted sends and drops a send once the watcher records it (OnChain or Sent). TestPendingListsSignedSendsUntilTheWatcherRecordsThem covers unsigned, another user's profile and recorded. Web: Sending rows come first, are dropped when a recorded row has the same hash, are hidden by search and Received, keep amounts in base units, and submit invalidates PendingSends. Lock: the review no longer unlocks; progress holds the lock until the server has the hash; only 404/422 unlock. Must fix: send-lock.test.tsx:101-103 asserts the network-failure case right after submit is called, before its rejection is handled. In a scratch copy where every error set refused, the test still passed 2 of 6 runs, so the network-failure guard is not reliably tested. Wait for the rejection to be handled (a flag set when the mock rejects and is caught, or a macrotask) before asserting holding is still true. Should fix: DESIGN.md:1099 still says the sheet is locked only while Privy signs; it now stays locked until the server holds the hash and opens on a 404/422 refusal. DESIGN.md:77 lists pending badges without Sending. No web test covers the Sending merge (dedupe by hash, search/Received hiding). Commands: go test ./internal/send/ ./internal/httpapi/tests/ -count=1 ok; vitest run src/features/send src/features/transactions 17 passed; harness check typecheck lint docs-check passed.
